Your brain gives you a fever on purpose 🌡️

When germs get in, white blood cells release chemicals called pyrogens, and the thermostat in your hypothalamus resets higher. Normal suddenly feels cold, so you shiver to make heat and blood moves away from your skin to keep it in. The extra heat makes it harder for many germs to grow and helps your immune defenses.

See a doctor if it goes above 39.4°C (103°F), lasts more than 3 days, or comes with a stiff neck or confusion.

Sources: MSD Manual, Cleveland Clinic, NHS.

A fever is not your body breaking. When germs get in, white blood cells release pyrogens and the thermostat in your hypothalamus resets higher, so you shiver and feel cold until you reach the new temperature. The heat makes it harder for many germs to grow and helps your immune defenses. See a doctor if it goes above 39.4°C (103°F), lasts more than 3 days, or comes with a stiff neck or confusion.
